# Nex backend — Phase 2 sync API.
# Every variable below is validated at boot by src/env.ts. The process exits
# with code 1 on invalid configuration rather than starting in a broken state.

# Required. No fallback: an unset value fails validation instead of silently
# connecting to a libpq default database.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/nex

# Optional.
PORT=4000
NODE_ENV=development

# Comma-separated origin allow-list for CORS. Empty means "no browser origin
# is permitted", which is the correct default for a native-client-only API.
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=

# "1" enables POST /sync/test/reset. Never set this in production.
NEX_TEST_MODE=0

# "1" runs pending migrations at boot. Production should leave this at 0 and
# run `npm run migrate` as an explicit deploy step (see docs/06-development.md).
NEX_AUTO_MIGRATE=0

# Sync tuning.
SYNC_PAGE_SIZE=500
PAIRING_CODE_TTL_SECONDS=600

# Tombstones are purged once every known device has pulled past them AND this
# many days have elapsed.
TOMBSTONE_RETENTION_DAYS=30
PURGE_INTERVAL_MINUTES=60

files.note: Explicit deploy step. Migration is no longer a boot side effect in production.
Idempotent so it can be adopted by a database that was already created by the old inline migrate().

-- 0005_tag_identity.sql — make the tag natural key the merge key.
--
-- tags.name carried a global UNIQUE constraint while the upsert conflicted on
-- (id). Offline-first guarantees the same name will be minted with different
-- UUIDs on different devices, so the second push hit a 23505 and broke sync for
-- that user permanently.
--
-- Identity is now (user_id, lower(name)). Case-variant duplicates created
-- before this migration are folded into the lexically-smallest id.

-- 1. Re-point note_tags rows at the surviving tag id.
WITH canonical AS (
  SELECT user_id, lower(name) AS norm, MIN(id) AS keep_id
    FROM tags
   GROUP BY user_id, lower(name)
), dupes AS (
  SELECT t.id AS drop_id, c.keep_id
    FROM tags t
    JOIN canonical c
      ON c.user_id = t.user_id AND c.norm = lower(t.name)
   WHERE t.id <> c.keep_id
)
INSERT INTO note_tags (note_id, tag_id)
SELECT nt.note_id, d.keep_id
  FROM note_tags nt
  JOIN dupes d ON d.drop_id = nt.tag_id
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- 2. Delete the now-redundant tag rows (note_tags cascades).
WITH canonical AS (
  SELECT user_id, lower(name) AS norm, MIN(id) AS keep_id
    FROM tags
   GROUP BY user_id, lower(name)
)
DELETE FROM tags t
 USING canonical c
 WHERE c.user_id = t.user_id
   AND c.norm = lower(t.name)
   AND t.id <> c.keep_id;

-- 3. Swap the constraint.
ALTER TABLE tags DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS tags_name_key;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_tags_user_name_ci
  ON tags (user_id, lower(name));

# Multi-stage build. Produces a deployable artifact from the emitting
# tsconfig.build.json — previously the project had noEmit: true, no build
# script and no container, so there was no path from a green CI run to a
# running server.

FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY tsconfig.json tsconfig.build.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=4000

# Migrations are read from disk at runtime by the file-based runner.
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/package.json ./package.json
COPY src/db/migrations ./dist/db/migrations

USER node
EXPOSE 4000

# Readiness, not liveness: an instance that cannot reach PostgreSQL must not be
# reported healthy.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+(process.env.PORT||4000)+'/health/ready').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"

# Run migrations as an explicit deploy step before starting:
#   docker run --rm --env-file .env nex-backend npm run migrate
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

node_modules
dist
npm-debug.log*
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
*.test.ts
coverage
.git
.gitignore
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
README.md

name: nex_client
description: >-
  Nex client. A single Flutter app target that builds to Android, Windows and
  (later) iOS — see ADR-024.
publish_to: "none"
version: 0.1.1

# Member of the root pub workspace: one shared resolution, one lockfile.
resolution: workspace

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0
  flutter: ">=3.35.0 <4.0.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
  file_selector: ^1.0.3
  image_picker: ^1.1.2
  # Pinned to the version flutter_localizations resolves against on 3.35.x.
  # "any" delegated the constraint entirely to whatever Flutter stable was
  # installed at build time.
  intl: ^0.20.2
  just_audio: ^0.10.0
  # Endorses the Windows implementation. Without it every playback call throws
  # MissingPluginException on a first-class v1 target.
  just_audio_windows: ^0.2.2
  # Declared explicitly: the app is the composition root and owns the SQLite
  # database. It used to arrive silently through nex_core's re-export.
  nex_core:
    path: ../../packages/core
  nex_data:
    path: ../../packages/data
  nex_ui:
    path: ../../packages/ui
  path: ^1.9.1
  path_provider: ^2.1.5
  record: ^6.1.1
  shared_preferences: ^2.3.3
  sqlite3: ^2.7.5
  sqlite3_flutter_libs: ^0.5.28
  uuid: ^4.5.1

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^5.0.0

flutter:
  uses-material-design: true
  generate: true

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Cleartext is denied globally. The only exceptions are the loopback aliases a
  developer needs to reach a backend running on the host machine:

    10.0.2.2   Android emulator alias for the host
    127.0.0.1  desktop local development
    localhost  desktop local development

  A blanket android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" would have permitted plaintext
  sync to any host, which contradicts the product's privacy positioning.
-->
<network-security-config>
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" />

    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true">
        <domain includeSubdomains="false">10.0.2.2</domain>
        <domain includeSubdomains="false">127.0.0.1</domain>
        <domain includeSubdomains="false">localhost</domain>
    </domain-config>
</network-security-config>

files.note: PATCH ONLY — this blob returned an empty body during the audit, so replacing it wholesale would destroy the capture-widget receiver and share-intent filters that CaptureWidgetProvider.kt and MainActivity.kt depend on. Apply the two edits below to your existing file.
files.content:
<!--
  Apply these two edits to apps/client/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml.

  Do NOT replace the whole file. It contains the capture-widget receiver and the
  share-intent filters, which were not part of the audited read set.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. Ensure the INTERNET permission is declared once, above <application>.
     (Required for sync; harmless if already present.)

       <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2. Add these two attributes to the existing <application> element, keeping
     every attribute already there unchanged:

       android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"
       android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"

     So the opening tag becomes, for example:

       <application
           android:label="Nex"
           android:name="[dollar]{applicationName}"
           android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"
           android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"
           android:usesCleartextTraffic="false">

     (Replace "[dollar]" above with a literal dollar sign — it is escaped here
     only so this note renders correctly.)

  Everything else in the file stays exactly as it is.
-->

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Themed-icon monochrome layer (Android 13+).

  This file used to be a byte-identical copy of nex_icon_foreground.xml - same
  git blob SHA, same 298 bytes. The system tints the monochrome layer with the
  wallpaper accent colour and expects a flat, alpha-only silhouette; a coloured
  vector renders as a solid tinted blob or disappears entirely depending on the
  active theme.

  fillColor MUST be a single opaque colour (conventionally #FFFFFF). All shape
  information must come from the geometry of the path itself.

  TODO(design): replace pathData with the real Nex mark, exported as a single
  merged path at 108x108 with the 72x72 safe zone respected.
-->
<vector xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:width="108dp"
    android:height="108dp"
    android:viewportWidth="108"
    android:viewportHeight="108">
    <path
        android:fillColor="#FFFFFF"
        android:pathData="M36,30 L36,78 L44,78 L44,46 L64,78 L72,78 L72,30 L64,30 L64,62 L44,30 Z" />
</vector>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<adaptive-icon xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">

name: nex_core
description: >-
  Nex core domain layer. Platform-agnostic, pure Dart, zero Flutter dependency,
  zero storage dependency. Dependency rule (06-development.md):
  apps/* -> packages/core and packages/data -> packages/core. Core is the
  bottom of the graph and depends on nothing in this repository.
publish_to: "none"
version: 0.1.0

resolution: workspace

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0

dependencies:
  crypto: ^3.0.6
  uuid: ^4.5.1
  # nex_data removed. Core used to depend on the storage layer AND re-export it
  # wholesale, which inverted the documented layering.

dev_dependencies:
  lints: ^5.0.0
  test: ^1.25.0

name: nex_data
description: >-
  Nex local-first data layer. Pure Dart, zero Flutter dependency. Implements the
  ports declared in nex_core: owns the schema, the SQLite repository and (from
  v2) the sync client.
publish_to: "none"
version: 0.1.0

resolution: workspace

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0

dependencies:
  archive: ^4.0.2
  crypto: ^3.0.6
  http: ^1.2.2
  # The arrow is inverted: data now depends on core, not the reverse. Core owns
  # the models and the port interfaces; this package implements them.
  nex_core:
    path: ../core
  path: ^1.9.1
  sqlite3: ^2.7.5
  uuid: ^4.5.1

dev_dependencies:
  lints: ^5.0.0
  test: ^1.25.0

name: nex_ui
description: >-
  Shared Flutter widget and design-token package for Nex. Depends on the core
  domain models only — never on the storage or transport layer.
publish_to: "none"
version: 0.1.0

resolution: workspace

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0
  flutter: ">=3.35.0 <4.0.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  # After the re-export removal this is pure domain: no sqlite3, no archive,
  # no http in the design system's dependency closure.
  nex_core:
    path: ../core
  intl: ^0.20.2
  path: ^1.9.1

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^5.0.0

flutter:
  uses-material-design: true

name: nex_ai
description: >-
  Nex optional AI leaf (v3+). Re-exports Core AI contracts/adapters. Deleting
  this package must leave core/data/client compiling (see docs/09-ai.md).
publish_to: "none"
version: 0.1.0

resolution: workspace

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0

dependencies:
  nex_core:
    path: ../core

dev_dependencies:
  lints: ^5.0.0
  nex_data:
    path: ../data
  test: ^1.25.0

files.note: Dart pub workspace root. Requires Dart 3.6+; produces one shared resolution and one lockfile.
files.content:
# Dart pub workspace root.
#
# Before this file, each of the five Dart packages resolved independently and
# produced its own pubspec.lock, so a shared transitive dependency (crypto,
# uuid, path, sqlite3, lints) could resolve to a different version in each
# package with nothing to detect the skew. The only place the full graph was
# exercised was CI, across five hand-written jobs.
#
# One `dart pub get` at the root now resolves every member together.
name: nex_workspace
publish_to: "none"

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0

workspace:
  - apps/client
  - packages/ai
  - packages/core
  - packages/data
  - packages/ui

files.note: Single source of truth consumed by every Flutter job via flutter-version-file.

files.content:
# Mirrors the CI jobs one-to-one so `make check` reproduces the pipeline
# locally. Every CI job below reduces to one of these targets.

.PHONY: check check-dart check-ui check-client check-backend \
        fmt clean bootstrap backend-dev migrate

bootstrap:
	dart pub get
	cd apps/backend && npm ci

# Pure Dart packages: proves core and data carry zero Flutter dependency.
check-dart:
	cd packages/core && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart test
	cd packages/data && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart test
	cd packages/ai   && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart test

check-ui:
	cd packages/ui && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test

check-client:
	cd apps/client && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test

check-backend:
	cd apps/backend && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test

check: check-dart check-ui check-client check-backend

fmt:
	dart format apps/client packages
	cd apps/backend && npx prettier --write "src/**/*.ts"

backend-dev:
	cd apps/backend && npm run start:dev

migrate:
	cd apps/backend && npm run migrate:dev

clean:
	flutter clean || true
	rm -rf apps/backend/dist apps/backend/node_modules

files.note: Single source of truth for merge semantics. Both the TypeScript and Dart suites iterate this corpus.

files.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  # Callable from release.yml so a tag cannot ship unverified code.
  workflow_call:

# Pushing three commits to a PR used to run three full matrices in parallel,
# including a 2x-billed Windows runner.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Phase 1 pipeline (11-build-prompt.md): Dart analyze/lint, dart test for
# packages/* (including SQLite/FTS integration), Flutter analyze/test/build for
# apps/client, and backend lint/typecheck/test.

jobs:
  dart-packages:
    name: Pure Dart packages (analyze + test, no Flutter SDK)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package: [core, data, ai]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/${{ matrix.package }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: "3.9.0"
      # sqlite3 Dart FFI needs the system library (packages/data uses package:sqlite3).
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-0 libsqlite3-dev
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-
      # Proves packages/core and packages/data carry zero Flutter dependency:
      # this job never installs Flutter.
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart analyze --fatal-infos
      - run: dart test

  core-boundary:
    name: packages/core must not re-export the storage layer
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Assert nex_core does not re-export nex_data
        run: |
          if grep -q "export 'package:nex_data" packages/core/lib/nex_core.dart; then
            echo "::error::packages/core must not re-export packages/data (06-development.md dependency rule)"
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Assert nex_core does not depend on nex_data
        run: |
          if grep -q "nex_data" packages/core/pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::packages/core must not depend on nex_data — the arrow is data -> core"
            exit 1
          fi

  flutter-ui-package:
    name: packages/ui (analyze + test + dependency closure)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/ui
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - run: flutter pub get
      # A design system must not carry native FFI, archive or HTTP transitively.
      - name: Assert the design system has no storage dependency
        run: |
          flutter pub deps --style=compact --no-dev | tee deps.txt
          if grep -Eq '(^|[[:space:]])(sqlite3|archive|http)[[:space:]]' deps.txt; then
            echo "::error::packages/ui must not depend on the storage or transport layer"
            exit 1
          fi
      - run: flutter analyze --fatal-infos
      - run: flutter test

  client-android:
    name: apps/client (analyze + test + Android build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 35
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
      - run: flutter pub get
      - run: flutter analyze --fatal-infos
      - run: flutter test
      - run: flutter build apk --debug

  client-windows:
    name: apps/client (Windows desktop build + platform tests)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - run: flutter config --enable-windows-desktop
      - run: flutter pub get
      # Plugin availability is a runtime concern: building alone hid the fact
      # that just_audio had no Windows implementation.
      - run: flutter test test/platform_capability_test.dart
      - run: flutter build windows --debug

  client-ios:
    name: apps/client (iOS compile check, no signing)
    runs-on: macos-14
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Only on push — macOS minutes are billed at 10x.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_call'
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - run: flutter pub get
      # The ios/ directory is committed but was never built, so its Podfile,
      # deployment target and plugin registrations drifted silently on every
      # dependency change.
      - run: flutter build ios --debug --no-codesign

  backend:
    name: apps/backend (lint + typecheck + test + build + boot)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          # --experimental-strip-types requires 22.6+. The engines field and
          # this runner must agree with the start script.
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/backend/package-lock.json
      # npm ci fails when package.json and the lockfile disagree; npm install
      # silently rewrote the lockfile instead.
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build
      # Proves the documented production entry point actually starts.
      - name: Smoke test the built artifact
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/nex
          PORT: "4100"
        run: |
          node dist/index.js > "$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke.pid"
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:4100/health/live | grep -q '"phase":2'; then
              kill "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke.pid")" || true
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          echo "::error::built backend did not become live"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke.log"
          exit 1

  merge-conformance:
    name: Merge conformance (TypeScript and Dart agree)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/backend/package-lock.json
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: "3.9.0"
      - name: TypeScript implementation
        working-directory: apps/backend
        run: |
          npm ci
          npx tsx --test src/services/merge.conformance.test.ts
      - name: Dart implementation
        working-directory: packages/core
        run: |
          dart pub get
          dart test test/merge_conformance_test.dart

  sync-integration:
    name: Phase 2 sync matrix (live SyncClient + PostgreSQL)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: nex
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/backend/package-lock.json
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: "3.9.0"
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-0 libsqlite3-dev

      - name: Install backend deps
        working-directory: apps/backend
        run: npm ci

      - name: Apply migrations
        working-directory: apps/backend
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/nex
        run: npm run migrate:dev

      # Seed one user + one device token so the suite can authenticate. The API
      # is no longer open, so the matrix must pair like a real client.
      - name: Seed test tenant
        env:
          PGPASSWORD: postgres
        run: |
          TOKEN="ci-integration-token"
          HASH=$(printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
          psql -h localhost -U postgres -d nex -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<SQL
          INSERT INTO users (id) VALUES ('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000')
            ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
          INSERT INTO devices (device_id, user_id, label, token_hash)
          VALUES ('ci-device-a', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000', 'ci', '$HASH')
            ON CONFLICT (device_id) DO UPDATE SET token_hash = EXCLUDED.token_hash;
          SQL
          echo "SYNC_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # setsid detaches the server from this step's shell, which exits as soon
      # as the step finishes. A bare "&" left it orphaned and its logs lost.
      - name: Start Phase 2 backend
        working-directory: apps/backend
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/nex
          PORT: "4000"
          NEX_TEST_MODE: "1"
          NEX_AUTO_MIGRATE: "0"
        run: |
          setsid npx tsx src/index.ts > "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
          echo $! > "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend.pid"
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:4000/health/ready | grep -q '"database":"up"'; then
              echo "backend ready"
              break
            fi
            if [ "$i" -eq 60 ]; then
              echo "::error::backend failed to become ready"
              cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend.log"
              exit 1
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

      - name: Run mandatory 6-row sync matrix
        working-directory: packages/data
        env:
          RUN_SYNC_MATRIX: "1"
          SYNC_BASE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:4000
          SYNC_BEARER_TOKEN: ${{ env.SYNC_TOKEN }}
          SYNC_DEVICE_ID: ci-device-a
        run: |
          dart pub get
          dart test test/sync_matrix_test.dart

      - name: Backend log
        if: always()
        run: cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend.log" || true

      - name: Stop backend
        if: always()
        run: kill "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true

  # Permanent Phase 3 proof (09-ai.md / 11-build-prompt.md): packages/ai must be
  # deletable without breaking core/data/ui/client.
  #
  # The old version only checked apps/client and only rebuilt apps/client, which
  # made it close to a tautology: every AI contract the client consumes lives in
  # packages/core and cannot be deleted. It now asserts the real invariant and
  # rebuilds the whole downstream graph.
  ai-deletion-proof:
    name: packages/ai deletion proof (downstream graph still builds)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-0 libsqlite3-dev

      - name: Assert nothing outside packages/ai imports nex_ai
        run: |
          if grep -Rn --include='*.dart' "package:nex_ai/" apps packages --exclude-dir=ai; then
            echo "::error::only packages/ai may import package:nex_ai (09-ai.md)"
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -q 'nex_ai' apps/client/pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::apps/client must not list nex_ai (09-ai.md)"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Delete packages/ai
        run: |
          rm -rf packages/ai
          # Drop the member from the workspace so pub can still resolve.
          sed -i '/- packages\/ai/d' pubspec.yaml

      - name: Downstream graph still resolves, analyzes, tests and builds
        run: |
          cd packages/core && dart pub get && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart test && cd -
          cd packages/data && dart pub get && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart test && cd -
          cd packages/ui   && flutter pub get && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test && cd -
          cd apps/client   && flutter pub get && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test && flutter build apk --debug

name: Release

# Builds a signed Android App Bundle + split APKs and a Windows Inno Setup
# installer, and attaches them to a GitHub Release. Triggered by version tags or
# manually.
#
# Required repo secrets (one-time; never commit the keystore):
#   ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64, ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD,
#   ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Tag to build (e.g. v1.2.3 or v0.0.1-test)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Tag push -> github.ref_name; manual run -> inputs.tag
  RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  # A tag used to ship straight to a public Release without ever running
  # analyze, tests, or the backend suite: ci.yml triggers on branches, and tags
  # do not match branches.
  verify:
    name: Full verification suite
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  build-android:
    name: Android release bundle + APKs
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          # Pinned in .flutter-version so a stable bump cannot silently change
          # the compiler, AGP defaults or the Android embedding mid-release.
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4

      - name: Require Android signing secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          for name in ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              echo "::error::$name secret missing — add it under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions (see docs/06-development.md § Cutting a Release). Refusing to ship an unsigned/debug APK as a release artifact."
              missing=1
            fi
          done
          exit $missing

      - name: Decode keystore
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          echo "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" | base64 -d > android/app/nex-release.keystore
          test -s android/app/nex-release.keystore

      - name: Write key.properties
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "storePassword=$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
            echo "keyPassword=$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
            echo "keyAlias=$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
            echo "storeFile=nex-release.keystore"
          } > android/key.properties
          test -s android/key.properties

      - name: Resolve version from tag
        id: ver
        run: |
          TAG="${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}"
          VERSION="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building Android release for version=$VERSION"

      - name: Verify the tag matches pubspec.yaml
        run: |
          PUBSPEC=$(grep -m1 '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d'+' -f1)
          BASE=$(echo "${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}" | cut -d'-' -f1)
          if [ "$PUBSPEC" != "$BASE" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag version $BASE does not match pubspec.yaml version $PUBSPEC"
            exit 1
          fi

      # github.run_number is scoped to the workflow FILE: renaming or recreating
      # release.yml resets it to 1. Play requires versionCode to increase
      # strictly and forever, so it must be derived from the semantic version.
      - name: Compute monotonic versionCode
        id: vc
        run: |
          BASE=$(echo "${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}" | cut -d'-' -f1)
          IFS=. read -r MA MI PA <<< "$BASE"
          CODE=$(( MA * 1000000 + MI * 1000 + PA ))
          echo "code=$CODE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "versionCode=$CODE"

      - run: flutter pub get

      - name: Build App Bundle (Play) and split APKs (direct download)
        run: |
          flutter build appbundle --release \
            --build-name=${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }} \
            --build-number=${{ steps.vc.outputs.code }}
          flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi \
            --build-name=${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }} \
            --build-number=${{ steps.vc.outputs.code }}

      - name: Collect release assets
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab \
            "dist/Nex-${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}.aab"
          for abi in armeabi-v7a arm64-v8a x86_64; do
            src="build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-$abi-release.apk"
            [ -f "$src" ] && cp "$src" "dist/Nex-${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}-$abi.apk"
          done
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: android
          path: apps/client/dist/*

  build-windows:
    name: Windows Inno Setup installer
    needs: verify
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version-file: .flutter-version
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - run: flutter config --enable-windows-desktop
      - run: flutter pub get

      - name: Resolve version from tag
        id: ver
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $tag = "${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}"
          $version = $tag -replace '^v',''
          "version=$version" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append
          Write-Host "Building Windows release for version=$version"

      - name: Compute monotonic versionCode
        id: vc
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $base = ("${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}" -split '-')[0]
          $p = $base -split '\.'
          $code = [int]$p[0] * 1000000 + [int]$p[1] * 1000 + [int]$p[2]
          "code=$code" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append

      - name: Build Windows release
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          flutter build windows --release `
            --build-name=${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }} `
            --build-number=${{ steps.vc.outputs.code }}

      - name: Install Inno Setup
        shell: pwsh
        run: choco install innosetup -y --no-progress

      - name: Build installer
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $version = "${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}"
          $iscc = "C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe"
          if (-not (Test-Path $iscc)) {
            throw "Inno Setup ISCC.exe not found at $iscc"
          }
          & $iscc "windows\installer\nex.iss" "/DAppVersion=$version"
          Get-ChildItem "windows\installer\Output\*.exe" | Format-Table Name, Length

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: windows-installer
          path: apps/client/windows/installer/Output/*.exe

  publish-release:
    name: Publish GitHub Release
    needs: [build-android, build-windows]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

      - name: List artifacts
        run: find . -type f -printf '%p %s bytes\n'

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        # Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA: this job holds
        # contents: write, so a compromised mutable tag would be able to push
        # to the repository.
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@01570a1f39cb168c169c802c3bceb9e93fb10974 # v2.1.0
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
          name: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
          # Manual verification runs (workflow_dispatch) publish as draft so a
          # test tag does not look like a production release.
          draft: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: |
            android/*.aab
            android/*.apk
            windows-installer/*.exe

version: 2

# Dependency drift used to accumulate silently across three ecosystems until an
# upgrade became a large, risky batch — just_audio 0.9.x and flutter_lints 4.x
# were already behind by the time of the audit.
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /apps/backend
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      backend-dev:
        dependency-type: development
      backend-prod:
        dependency-type: production
        update-types: [minor, patch]

  - package-ecosystem: pub
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      day: monday
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5

  - package-ecosystem: gradle
    directory: /apps/client/android
    schedule:
      interval: monthly

  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3

# Default owner for anything not matched below.
*                                   @sanyzrn

# Correctness-critical: the sync protocol and its conformance corpus.
/apps/backend/src/services/         @sanyzrn
/apps/backend/src/db/migrations/    @sanyzrn
/packages/core/lib/sync/            @sanyzrn
/spec/merge-conformance.json        @sanyzrn

# Security boundary.
/apps/backend/src/middleware/       @sanyzrn
/apps/backend/src/routes/auth.ts    @sanyzrn

# Architectural decisions are binding — see docs/10-decisions.md.
/docs/10-decisions.md               @sanyzrn
/packages/core/lib/nex_core.dart    @sanyzrn
/packages/core/lib/ports/           @sanyzrn

# Release and signing.
/.github/workflows/                 @sanyzrn
/apps/client/android/app/build.gradle.kts  @sanyzrn

# Security Policy

## Threat model

Nex is local-first. In v1 all data lives on the user's device and never leaves
it. From v2 an optional sync server holds an encrypted-in-transit copy of notes
for the accounts that opt in. The assets we care about, in order:

1. **Note contents and media.** Users capture unfiltered thoughts. Disclosure is
   the worst possible outcome for this product.
2. **Device tokens.** A leaked device token grants full read/write to one
   account's corpus until it is revoked.
3. **Availability of capture.** Capture must work offline and must never be
   blocked by a network or server failure.

## Supported versions

Only the latest tagged release receives security fixes.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report privately via GitHub's **Report a vulnerability** button on the
Security tab, or by opening a draft security advisory. Do not open a public
issue.

Please include: affected component (client / backend / packages), the version or
commit, reproduction steps, and the impact you believe it has.

We aim to acknowledge within 72 hours and to ship a fix or a mitigation plan
within 30 days for anything rated high or critical.

## Scope

In scope: the Flutter client, the sync backend, the Dart packages, the release
pipeline, and the signing configuration.

Out of scope: findings that require a physically unlocked device with the app
already open; denial of service against a self-hosted backend the reporter
controls; and missing hardening headers on endpoints that hold no data.

## Handling secrets

The Android upload keystore and its passwords live only in GitHub Actions
secrets. They are never committed. `android/key.properties` and
`*.keystore` are gitignored, and CI release builds fail hard rather than
falling back to the debug key.

## What does this change?

<!-- One or two sentences. Link the issue or ADR if there is one. -->

## Why?

<!-- The single most common reason a contribution is declined is that it adds
     friction to capture, however good the code is. See docs/07-contributing.md. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` passes locally (analyze + tests for every package and the backend)
- [ ] Capture still requires zero mandatory fields and no Save button
- [ ] No new dependency added to `packages/core` or `packages/ui`
- [ ] If sync semantics changed, `spec/merge-conformance.json` has a new case
- [ ] If the schema changed, a numbered migration was added under `apps/backend/src/db/migrations/`
- [ ] If a decision was made that future readers would question, `docs/10-decisions.md` has an ADR

## Risk

<!-- What breaks if this is wrong? Can it lose a user's notes? -->

Sync API has no auth, authorization or tenancy
statusRows.note: Auth boundary, devices table, tokens and pairing are fully implemented and every query is user-scoped. Account signup/login is deliberately not implemented — the backend is documented as dormant until v2, so migration 0003 backfills existing rows to one legacy user. Provisioning real users is a product decision, not a bug fix.

Replace direct ImagePicker/openFile usage in apps/client/lib/screens with services.mediaPicker, and drive button visibility from mediaPicker.supportsCamera rather than Platform.is* checks.
Update assertions in apps/backend/src/services/merge.test.ts that expect a tombstone to retain content/media_uri — the merge now nulls the payload by design.
Replace the placeholder pathData in nex_icon_monochrome.xml with the real single-colour Nex silhouette from the design source, then verify under themed icons in light and dark mode.
Run `flutter pub get` at the repo root once (pub workspace) and commit the generated apps/client/pubspec.lock so application builds are reproducible.

deletions.reason: The directory now contains real migration files, so the placeholder is obsolete. Harmless if kept.
The directory contains merge.ts, sync-service.ts and purge.ts. Harmless if kept.

decisions.title: Auth scheme — opaque device bearer tokens, SHA-256 at rest
decisions.body: NEX-002 did not specify a token format. I chose a 256-bit opaque random token (base64url) issued per device at pairing time, stored only as a SHA-256 hash in devices.token_hash, and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Rationale: no JWT key management, instant revocation (set revoked_at), no clock dependency (which matters given NEX-005), and no PII in the token. Pairing uses a short-lived, single-use code generated on an already-trusted device via POST /auth/pairing-code and redeemed via POST /auth/pair.

decisions.title: Tenancy model — users + devices, single legacy user backfill
decisions.body: The schema had no owner concept. I added a users table and a devices table, and added user_id to notes, tags, media_objects and device_acks. Existing rows are backfilled to a single well-known legacy user id (00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000) so migration 0003 is safe on a populated database. Account creation itself (signup/login) is deliberately out of scope — the backend is documented as dormant until v2, so I provisioned the boundary without inventing an identity product.

decisions.title: Migration tool — in-house file runner, no new dependency
decisions.body: NEX-027 offered node-pg-migrate, dbmate, or an in-house runner. I built the in-house runner over the already-scaffolded src/db/migrations/ directory: a schema_migrations table, a pg advisory lock so concurrent replicas cannot race, one transaction per migration file, and lexical ordering by filename. Rationale: zero new runtime dependencies, no separate CLI toolchain in CI, and it reuses the directory the repo already created but never used.

decisions.title: Sync cursor — BIGSERIAL sequence, not a timestamp
decisions.body: NEX-005 required removing the Node/Postgres clock split. Rather than reconciling clocks, I eliminated the timestamp cursor entirely: notes and tags each get a monotonic seq column fed by a dedicated sequence, bumped on every write. The pull cursor is now an opaque integer. This also makes pagination (NEX-018) correct and makes the boundary condition unambiguous.

decisions.title: Express 4 retained, express-async-errors added
decisions.body: NEX-024 allowed either express-async-errors or an Express 5 upgrade. I kept Express 4.21.2 and added express-async-errors (3.1.1). Rationale: Express 5 changes router matching, req.query behaviour and error semantics — a migration that deserves its own change, not a side effect of an error-handling fix.

decisions.title: Tag identity — canonical by (user_id, lower(name)), server returns a remap
decisions.body: NEX-004 offered two options. I made name the merge key: the UNIQUE(name) constraint is dropped and replaced with UNIQUE(user_id, lower(name)), the upsert conflicts on that index, and /sync/push returns a tag_remap array of {client_id, canonical_id} so the client can rewrite its local note_tags rows. This preserves user intent (#Ideas and #ideas are one tag) and is the only option that converges without a coordinator.

decisions.title: Layer inversion — packages/data now depends on packages/core, not the reverse
decisions.body: NEX-010/NEX-033 required breaking the blanket re-export. Rather than leaving core depending on data and merely hiding it, I inverted the arrow: core owns the ports (NoteRepository, SyncPort, MediaPicker) and no longer depends on nex_data at all; data depends on core and implements the ports. This is what actually removes sqlite3 from the design system's dependency closure. The concrete classes inside packages/data need mechanical `implements` clauses added — see the deviation note on NEX-010.

decisions.title: NEX-042 — proof widened rather than contracts relocated
decisions.body: The fix offered two options: move the AI contracts out of core, or rename the job and widen it. I chose the second. Moving AIAdapter/EnrichmentService out of core would break every client import for a property that docs/09-ai.md only asserts about the optional leaf. Instead the job now asserts that nothing outside packages/ai imports package:nex_ai, and runs the full downstream suite (core, data, ui, client) after deletion — so it verifies a real invariant instead of a tautology.

decisions.title: Client DB access — long-lived worker isolate
decisions.body: NEX-020 required getting synchronous sqlite3 FFI off the UI isolate. I added NexDbWorker, a long-lived isolate that owns the database handle and exposes an async request/response API. Backup moved off the launch path into a throttled, policy-driven background task. The worker's command surface covers the operations the client composition root actually uses today; new repository calls must be added to the command enum.
